major_cooldowns.name: Rewind
major_cooldowns.usage_rule: Line up with the most dangerous damage moment of each fight, ideally right after a large raid hit so the 5-second retroactive heal-over-time refunds 33% of the damage just taken.

major_cooldowns.name: Dream Flight
major_cooldowns.usage_rule: Fly through a stacked group on a recurring damage event to deliver a large area heal plus a lengthy heal-over-time, fitting in as many uses as the fight allows.

major_cooldowns.name: Stasis
major_cooldowns.usage_rule: Pre-store three high-value spells (for example Dream Breath and Temporal Anomaly) in advance, then release the stored burst right before a known heavy damage event, optionally pairing with Tip the Scales and Temporal Burst haste.

major_cooldowns.name: Tip the Scales
major_cooldowns.usage_rule: Use to make your next empowered spell instant at maximum rank, commonly paired with Stasis and the Temporal Burst haste window for a large instant healing payoff.

major_cooldowns.name: Emerald Communion
major_cooldowns.usage_rule: Channel during a lull when you can stand still to restore mana and deliver sustained group healing; this is a talent choice so absent casts are not necessarily an error.

defensives.name: Obsidian Scales
defensives.usage_rule: Press proactively before predictable burst damage to gain a flat damage reduction for the duration.

defensives.name: Renewing Blaze
defensives.usage_rule: Use ahead of a damage spike to recoup a large portion of the damage you take over the following window as healing.

defensives.name: Zephyr
defensives.usage_rule: Cast just before a telegraphed raid-wide AoE to reduce incoming area damage for yourself and nearby allies; scout useful spots when learning a fight.

defensives.name: Time Dilation
defensives.usage_rule: Apply to a single endangered target as a superb damage-reduction cooldown; its short cooldown means you can use it regularly rather than hoarding it.

defensives.name: Cauterizing Flame
defensives.usage_rule: Use to remove a dispellable Bleed, Poison, Curse, or Disease and heal the target; it does not trigger its cooldown when nothing is removed, so it can be pre-stored in Stasis for a mass cleanse.

rules.action: Press Temporal Anomaly the moment it comes off cooldown to generate Echo buffs across the group and refresh its absorb; this is your most powerful spell and the core of your throughput.

rules.description: Consume Echo buffs with the right spell
rules.action: Consume your Echo buffs with Merithra's Blessing (or Reversion as a backup) as Chronowarden, or Reversion as Flameshaper; reserve Verdant Embrace for moments that need a large per-target absorb or heal.

rules.description: Cast Dream Breath after consuming Echoes
rules.action: Cast Dream Breath regularly but only after you have consumed your Echo buffs, so the buffs are spent on a stronger spell rather than wasted on Dream Breath.

rules.description: Pre-pull Temporal Anomaly and Stasis ramp
rules.action: Cast Temporal Anomaly a few seconds before the pull to enter with Echo buffs, and pre-store a Stasis ramp so you can release a large heal at the first major damage event.
Layer Rewind, Dream Flight, and Stasis over the most dangerous moments of each fight rather than holding them just in case; banked cooldowns cost mana and risk avoidable deaths.
Cast Echo whenever you have Essence available and spend Essence Bursts on Emerald Blossom so you never waste either resource; with Twin Echoes, weave Emerald Blossom to empower your next Echo casts.

rules.description: Manage mana around the damage pattern
rules.action: Avoid dumping half your mana in the opening Bloodlust minute; align Temporal Anomaly with real damage and skip casts during quiet windows to keep mana for the whole fight.

rules.description: Stand central to cover the 30 yard range
rules.action: Position centrally to offset your reduced 30-yard healing range, and use Hover, Verdant Embrace, Rescue, and Zephyr to reposition or pre-place a heal-over-time on targets drifting out of range.

source_summary: Preservation Evoker concentrates its throughput in short cooldowns and pre-planned ramps: Temporal Anomaly is pressed on cooldown to seed Echo buffs that are then consumed by a stronger spell, while Dream Breath fills the gaps. Major cooldowns like Stasis, Dream Flight, and Rewind are pre-planned and layered over the fight's most dangerous moments rather than held in reserve, and Stasis can bank an entire burst before a known damage event. Mana discipline and central positioning to cover the spec's reduced 30-yard range are the defining constraints on optimal play.
